claims.sentence: NHS inform lists asthma attacks, pneumonia and heart failure among the likely causes of sudden breathlessness.
claims.evidence: NHS inform page lists asthma attack, pneumonia, heart failure among causes of sudden breathlessness.

claims.sentence: Less common sudden causes include a severe allergic reaction, a collapsed lung and a blood clot in the lung.
claims.evidence: NHS inform lists allergic reaction, pneumothorax and pulmonary embolism, but retrieved text does not call them 'less common'.
claims.newSentence: NHS inform also lists a severe allergic reaction, a collapsed lung and a blood clot in the lung as possible causes of sudden breathlessness.

claims.sentence: A collapsed lung, or pneumothorax, is a partial collapse caused by a small tear in the lung surface, and a pulmonary embolism is a blockage in one of the blood vessels in the lung.
claims.evidence: NHS inform text: pneumothorax is partial collapse of the lung caused by a small tear in the lung surface. No retrieved text defined pulmonary embolism as a blockage in a lung blood vessel (only 'blood clot in the lung'). Attribution to nhs.uk not shown.
claims.newSentence: A collapsed lung, or pneumothorax, is a partial collapse of the lung caused by a small tear in the lung surface.

claims.sentence: Breathlessness that lasts a long time is commonly linked to obesity, being unfit, poorly controlled asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), anaemia, heart failure and heart rhythm problems.
claims.evidence: Retrieved NHS text lists COPD, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, heart failure, lung cancer, asthma, chest infection, being overweight and smoking. Being unfit, anaemia and heart rhythm problems were not retrieved; 'commonly' not supported.
claims.newSentence: The NHS lists several possible causes of breathlessness, including COPD, scarring of the lungs, heart failure, asthma, chest infections and being overweight.

claims.sentence: In heart failure, fluid builds up in the lungs and makes breathing harder.
claims.evidence: NHS inform: heart failure leads to a build-up of fluid inside the lungs, which makes breathing more difficult.

claims.sentence: A panic attack or anxiety can make a person breathe fast or deeply, which is called hyperventilating.
claims.evidence: Panic attack / hyperventilation not found in any retrieved text.

claims.sentence: Sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, in which the airways narrow and make extra sticky mucus, causing wheeze and cough.
claims.evidence: NHS inform: sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, difficult to move air in and out of airways. Narrowing, sticky mucus, wheeze and cough not found in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: Sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, which makes it difficult to move air in and out of the airways.

claims.sentence: Typical COPD symptoms include increasing breathlessness when active, a persistent cough with phlegm and frequent chest infections.
claims.evidence: No retrieved text gave COPD symptom list (ledger itself says COPD page was not returned).

claims.sentence: The NHS lists breathlessness as the most common symptom of heart failure; it may happen after activity or at rest, may be worse when lying down, and may wake a person at night.
claims.evidence: NHS heart failure symptoms page: breathlessness most common; during activity or at rest; may be worse lying down; may wake at night.

claims.sentence: It lists tiredness, swollen ankles and legs, and feeling lightheaded or fainting as other heart failure symptoms.
claims.evidence: Same page: tiredness, swollen ankles and legs, lightheaded or fainting.

claims.sentence: An NHS trust leaflet says the most common symptom of a pulmonary embolism is breathlessness, with other symptoms including chest pain that is worse on breathing or coughing, cough, fever and coughing up blood.
claims.evidence: North Tees leaflet: breathlessness most common; chest pain worse on breathing or coughing; fever alongside cough. Coughing up blood came from a different trust leaflet (Royal Berkshire), not confirmed for this one.
claims.newSentence: An NHS trust leaflet says the most common symptom of a pulmonary embolism is breathlessness, with chest pain that is worse on breathing or coughing, and it also lists cough and fever.

claims.sentence: NHS inform says to call 999 or go to A&E for severe difficulty breathing, such as being unable to speak without pausing for breath.
claims.evidence: NHS inform: severe difficulty breathing (struggling to speak without pausing, gasping, choking) means call 999 or go to A&E.

claims.sentence: Chest tightness, or pain that spreads to the arms, back, neck or jaw, is also a reason to call 999.
claims.evidence: Chest tightness / pain to arms, back, neck, jaw as 999 reasons were found on the NHS (England) page and NHS 111 Wales, not confirmed on NHS inform. Wrong publisher.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says chest tightness or heaviness, or pain that spreads to the arms, back, neck or jaw, is also a reason to call 999 or go to A&E.

claims.sentence: A GP practice page adds sudden confusion, or lips or skin turning pale, blue or grey, to the signs that need an emergency response.
claims.evidence: Sudden confusion and pale, blue or grey lips or skin as 999/A&E signs are on the NHS shortness of breath page and NHS 111 Wales; Conwy practice page not returned, so attribution to a GP practice page is unverified.
claims.newSentence: The NHS adds sudden confusion, or lips or skin turning pale, blue or grey, to the signs for calling 999 or going to A&E.

claims.sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises that a person should not drive themselves to A&E but should ask someone to take them or call an ambulance.
claims.evidence: NHS 111 Wales: do not drive yourself; ask someone else to drive or call 999 for an ambulance.

claims.sentence: The NHS advises contacting NHS 111 or the GP urgently for worsening breathlessness, feeling sick, coughing up blood, or pain or swelling in one leg.
claims.evidence: Retrieved NHS text sends these symptoms (difficulty breathing, feeling or being sick, coughing up blood, pain or swelling in one leg) to NHS 111; 'or the GP' and 'worsening breathlessness' were not in that list. Changes route to care.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says to contact NHS 111 for difficulty breathing, feeling or being sick, coughing up blood, or pain or swelling in one leg.

claims.sentence: NHS inform says breathlessness that starts suddenly should be seen urgently by a GP because it may point to a problem with the airways or heart.
claims.evidence: NHS inform: contact GP practice if breathlessness is new or unexplained. 'Urgently' and the 'airways or heart' reasoning not found for sudden breathlessness.
claims.newSentence: NHS inform advises contacting the GP practice if breathlessness is new or unexplained.

claims.sentence: For breathlessness that comes on slowly, NHS inform advises seeing a GP if it has lasted more than a month, gets worse with activity or lying down, or comes with swollen ankles.
claims.evidence: Summary of NHS page: see a GP if breathlessness lasts longer than a month, worsens with activity or lying down, or comes with swollen ankles. Attributed to NHS inform in the draft, but found on the NHS page.
claims.newSentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if breathlessness has lasted longer than a month, gets worse with normal activity or when lying down, or comes with swollen ankles.

claims.sentence: A GP will usually ask when the breathlessness started, what brings it on and whether lying down makes it worse.
claims.evidence: Not found as a GP-questions list. NHS inform asks whether it came on suddenly or slowly and whether anything triggered it such as exercise.
claims.newSentence: NHS inform's guidance asks whether breathlessness came on suddenly or slowly and whether anything triggered it, such as exercise.

claims.sentence: An NHS England pathway for persistent breathlessness lists blood tests, an ECG, a chest X-ray and spirometry among the first tests.
claims.evidence: NHS England tool (chronic breathlessness, over 8 weeks) lists ECG, chest X-ray and spirometry as first-line; blood tests not confirmed for this tool (NT-proBNP was in a different regional pathway).
claims.newSentence: An NHS England pathway for persistent breathlessness lists an ECG, a chest X-ray and spirometry among the first-line tests.

claims.sentence: Spirometry is a breathing test that measures how much air a person can blow out and how fast.
claims.evidence: Trivial definition.

claims.sentence: If the cause is still unclear, the same pathway lists further tests such as a CT scan of the chest, an echocardiogram and ambulatory ECG monitoring.
claims.evidence: Retrieved text: ECG showing atrial fibrillation prompts cardiology assessment including echocardiography; further investigation planned at a multidisciplinary meeting. CT scan and ambulatory ECG monitoring not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: The same pathway says an ECG showing atrial fibrillation with breathlessness should prompt a heart specialist assessment, including an echocardiogram.

claims.sentence: Treatment depends on the cause.
claims.evidence: NHS 111 Wales / palliative page: treatment depends on what is causing the breathlessness.

claims.sentence: For COPD, treatment usually involves relieving symptoms with medicines such as inhalers, and pulmonary rehabilitation may help.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: COPD treatment usually centres on relieving symptoms with medication such as an inhaler; pulmonary rehabilitation may help. Exact page not clear from the blended summary.

claims.sentence: Heart failure is managed with lifestyle changes and medicines or surgery.
claims.evidence: NHS inform: lifestyle changes and medicines or surgery help the heart pump better and relieve breathlessness.

claims.sentence: A blood clot in the lung can be treated with anticoagulants, which are drugs that thin the blood.
claims.evidence: NHS inform cancer page: a clot can be treated with anticoagulants that thin the blood (cancer context). Better URL than nhs.uk page.

claims.sentence: One NHS leaflet describes relaxed breathing and pursed-lip breathing as techniques that can help a person regain control of their breathing.
claims.evidence: OUH leaflet text: pursed-lip breathing helps keep airways open longer and reduces work of breathing (useful in COPD). Relaxed breathing not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: NHS leaflets describe pursed-lip breathing as a technique that can help keep the airways open for longer and reduce the work of breathing, for example in COPD.

claims.sentence: Breathlessness has many causes, from asthma and anxiety to heart and lung disease, and severe difficulty breathing needs a 999 call.
claims.evidence: Anxiety as a cause not found in retrieved text; the rest (many causes, 999 for severe difficulty breathing) supported.
claims.newSentence: Breathlessness has many causes, from asthma and infections to heart and lung disease, and severe difficulty breathing needs a 999 call.

notes: All 8 searches used. Search summaries are blended and often do not name the page; attribution kept only where text matched. keyPoints[3] repeats the NHS '111 or the GP' route error and keyPoints[1] the asthma mucus/wheeze detail; fix to match edited body. Key point 3 on NHS inform 999 is fine. PE leaflet and Conwy page were not directly returned for some details. The NHS England pathway is for chronic (>8 weeks) breathlessness. NHS inform notes anaphylaxis is an emergency; the draft does not give a 999 route for it. Not checked against the site's own symptom/condition pages.
